content:
Returns a list of the top attack paths leading to critical assets. The response includes details about
each attack path, such as associated techniques, nodes, and metadata.
This endpoint supports advanced search capabilities, including filtering, sorting, and pagination.
For more information, see Top Attack Paths in the Exposure Management User Guide.
Requires the Basic [16] user role or the ATTACK_PATH_ANALYSIS.QUERY.SEARCH  custom role
privilege. See Roles and Permissions.
AUTHORIZATIONS:
cloud
QUERY PARAMETERS
integer
[ 100 .. 10000 ]
Default: 1000
The number of attack path records to retrieve. If omitted, the default
value is 1000 . The minimum value is 100  and the maximum value
is 10000 .
limit
integer
>= 0
Default: 0
The number of records to skip for offset-based pagination. If omitted,
the default value is 0 .
string ^[a-zA-Z_]+:(asc|desc)$
Example: sort=priority:desc
The property and direction to sort the results by, in the format
property:direction . For example: name:asc  or
priority:desc .
string
Default: "false"
Enum: "true"
"false"
Indicates whether or not to run the AI summarization for missing
paths.
Generative AI enables users to better understand attack paths and
their associated risk, and it provides additional insight into the assets
affected by the attack paths.
Note that enabling the AI summarization results in slower response
times.
REQUEST BODY SCHEMA:
application/json
optional
Filter conditions for searching attack paths. Filter operators can include nested conditions and
operators to create complex filtering logic.
One of
Single Filter
Multiple Filters
string
Enum: "priority"
"name"
"summary"
"steps"
"asset_exposure"
"blast_radius"
"asset_id"
"freetext"
"finding_id"
"technique"
"weakness_id"
"critical_asset"
"data_source"
"apa_aes"
"acr"
The property to filter on.
For example, you might filter by priority , name , or technique .
string
Enum: "eq"
"ne"
"gt"
"gte"
"lt"
"lte"
"contains"
"not_contains"
"in"
"not_in"
The comparison operator to apply to the filter. For example: eq , ne , etc.
Single String Value (string) or Array of Multiple String Values (strings) or Single
Integer Value (integer) or Array of Multiple Integer Values (integers) or Single
Boolean Value (boolean)
offset
sort
run_ai_summarization
property
operator
value
The value to use for comparison in the filter.
